                                           Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated re-         derstanding and reasoning capabilities. Despite their success,
                                        markable capabilities in aligning and understanding mul-       most VLMs focus on pairwise modality alignment, typically
                                        timodal signals, yet their potential to reason over struc-     between image and text, without modeling the relational
                                        tured data, where multimodal entities are connected through    structure that connects entities in real-world data. However,
                                        explicit relational graphs, remains largely underexplored.     such structural relationships are fundamental in many do-
                                        Unlocking this capability is crucial for real-world appli-     mains, including social networks [28, 36], recommendation
                                        cations such as social networks, recommendation systems,       systems [1, 23], and scientific knowledge graphs [29, 38],
                                        and scientific discovery, where multimodal information         where understanding inter-node dependencies is essential for
                                        is inherently structured. To bridge this gap, we present       reasoning beyond isolated pairs.
                                        GraphVLM, a systematic benchmark designed to evaluate             To capture such relationships, Multimodal graph learning
                                        and harness the capabilities of VLMs for multimodal graph      (MMGL) has emerged as a promising paradigm that com-
                                        learning (MMGL). GraphVLM investigates three comple-           bines heterogeneous node attributes with relational struc-
                                        mentary paradigms for integrating VLMs with graph rea-         tures, enabling richer representations for prediction and rec-
                                        soning: (1) VLM-as-Encoder, which enriches graph neu-          ommendation [37, 42]. Existing MMGL efforts largely fall
                                        ral networks through multimodal feature fusion; (2) VLM-       into two families: (1) GNN-based models [10, 12, 15, 34]
                                        as-Aligner, which bridges modalities in latent or linguistic   form the traditional paradigm, typically incorporating multi-
                                        space to facilitate LLM-based structured reasoning; and        modal node features extracted from pre-trained VLMs (e.g.,
                                        (3) VLM-as-Predictor, which directly employs VLMs as           CLIP) to enhance message passing; (2) LLM-based mod-
                                        multimodal backbones for graph learning tasks. Exten-          els [4–7, 21, 30, 31] reason over text-attributed graphs and
                                        sive experiments across six datasets from diverse domains      can be extended to multimodal settings by converting images
                                        demonstrate that VLMs enhance multimodal graph learn-          into textual or latent signals that LLMs can process.
                                        ing via all three roles. Among these paradigms, VLM-              Surprisingly, despite VLMs’ inherent strengths in multi-
                                        as-Predictor achieves the most substantial and consistent      modal alignment and cross-modal understanding, the third
                                        performance gains, revealing the untapped potential of vi-     paradigm–VLM-based models, directly employing VLMs
                                        sion–language models as a new foundation for multimodal        as reasoning backbones on multimodal graphs–remains
                                        graph learning. The benchmark code is publicly available       largely underexplored. This gap motivates a core research
                                        at https://github.com/oamyjin/GraphVLM .                       question: How and when can VLMs be effectively leveraged
                                                                                                       to perform multimodal graph learning?

   Across all settings, latent-space alignment consistently             in Movies (50.61%), Grocery (86.83%), and CDs (56.29%)
are achieved by LLaGA with latent-space alignment, while
Toys (80.00%) and Arts (89.79%) peak under MLaGA. This
improvement stems from the fact that latent-space alignment
allows multimodal embeddings to be further aligned through
learnable projectors in LLaGA or MLaGA during training,
enabling the model to better integrate structural cues and
reduce the noise or redundancy introduced by direct text
augmentation at the prompt level.

4.5. Comparative Analysis of VLM Roles (RQ4)
                                                                   5. Conclusion
After evaluating each MMGL paradigm and the respective
models, we combine all the paradigms to comprehensively            In this paper, we present GraphVLM, a comprehensive
assess and summarize the potential of VLMs for MMGL.               benchmark for multimodal graph learning (MMGL) that
    We compare the best performance of the original methods        evaluates state-of-the-art methods across six diverse graph
with VLM-enhanced models, highlighting the performance             datasets. Existing MMGL approaches are grouped into three
gains achieved through VLM integration. The results are            paradigms based on how Vision-Language Models (VLMs)
illustrated in Figure 4. To evaluate the effectiveness of struc-   are utilized: VLM-as-Encoder for GNN-based methods,
ture awareness across all approaches, we assess the extra per-     VLM-as-Aligner for LLM-based methods, and VLM-as-
formance gain provided by structure-aware methods in Fig-          Predictor, where VLMs are used as standalone predictors.
ure 5. This performance gain is calculated as the difference       Extensive experiments show that fine-tuning VLMs as pre-
between the highest accuracy achieved by structure-aware           dictors yields the most significant performance gains, even
methods and that achieved by structure-agnostic methods.           without explicit graph structural information, highlighting
✦ Finding 7: VLM-as-Predictor emerges as the most pow-             their potential as powerful backbones for MMGL. We hope
erful paradigm for MMGL, while VLM-as-Encoder and                  that GraphVLM serves as a fair and standardized benchmark
VLM-as-Aligner generally provide meaningful gains.                 to facilitate future research and foster continued innovation
    As shown in Figure 4, all three VLM roles bring bene-          in this rapidly evolving field.

Movies:    <image input> Given an image of a movie from the Amazon movies dataset , generate a concise and detailed
           summary. Focus on describing key visual concepts. Ensure the summary is informative and useful for understanding
           the product as described in user reviews, without losing critical details or introducing unnecessary information.
Toys:      <image input> Given an image of a toy from the Amazon toys dataset , generate a concise and detailed summary.
           Focus on describing key visual concepts. Ensure the summary is informative and useful for understanding the
           product as described in user reviews, without losing critical details or introducing unnecessary information.
Grocery:   <image input> Given an image of a grocery from the Amazon grocery dataset , generate a concise and detailed
           summary. Focus on describing key visual concepts. Ensure the summary is informative and useful for understanding
           the product as described in user reviews, without losing critical details or introducing unnecessary information.
CDs:       <image input> Given an image of a CD from the Amazon CD dataset , generate a concise and detailed summary.
           Focus on describing key visual concepts. Ensure the summary is informative and useful for understanding the
           product as described in user reviews, without losing critical details or introducing unnecessary information.
Arts:      <image input> Given an image of an artwork from the Amazon Art dataset , generate a concise and detailed
           summary. Focus on describing key visual concepts. Ensure the summary is informative and useful for understanding
           the product as described in user reviews, without losing critical details or introducing unnecessary information.
Reddit:    <image input> Given an image of a post from the Reddit dataset, generate a concise and detailed summary. Focus
           on describing key visual concepts. Ensure the summary is informative and useful for understanding the post as
           described in the caption, without losing critical details or introducing unnecessary information.

Movies:     Given the text information of a product from the Amazon movies dataset: <text information>. Image summary: <image
            summary>. Also given the information of co-purchased or co-reviewed products: text information: <neighbor text information>,
            image summary: <neighbor image summary> (or, if unavailable: ’No co-purchased or co-reviewed product information is
            available.’) Questions: Using the product’s title, description, and image summary provided above, along with any co-purchase or
            co-review data, generate a concise yet informative description of the product.
Toys:       Given the text information of a product from the Amazon toys dataset: <text information>. Image summary: <image summary>.
            Also given the information of co-purchased or co-reviewed products: text information: <neighbor text information>, image
            summary: <neighbor image summary> (or, if unavailable: ’No co-purchased or co-reviewed product information is available.’)
            Questions: Using the product’s title, description, and image summary provided above, along with any co-purchase or co-review
            data, generate a concise yet informative description of the product.
Grocery:    Given the text information of a product from the Amazon grocery dataset: <text information>. Image summary: <image
            summary>. Also given the information of co-purchased or co-reviewed products: text information: <neighbor text information>,
            image summary: <neighbor image summary> (or, if unavailable: ’No co-purchased or co-reviewed product information is
            available.’) Questions: Using the product’s title, description, and image summary provided above, along with any co-purchase or
            co-review data, generate a concise yet informative description of the product.
CDs:        Given the text information of a product from the Amazon CD dataset: <text information>. Image summary: <image summary>.
            Also given the information of co-purchased or co-reviewed products: text information: <neighbor text information>, image
            summary: <neighbor image summary> (or, if unavailable: ’No co-purchased or co-reviewed product information is available.’)
            Questions: Using the product’s title, description, and image summary provided above, along with any co-purchase or co-review
            data, generate a concise yet informative description of the product.
Arts:       Given the text information of a product from the Amazon Art dataset: <text information>. Image summary: <image summary>.
            Also given the information of co-purchased or co-reviewed products: text information: <neighbor text information>, image
            summary: <neighbor image summary> (or, if unavailable: ’No co-purchased or co-reviewed product information is available.’)
            Questions: Using the product’s title, description, and image summary provided above, along with any co-purchase or co-review
            data, generate a concise yet informative description of the product.
Reddit:     Given the text information of a post from the Reddit dataset: <text information>. Image summary: <image summary>. Also
            given the information of co-commented posts: text information: <neighbor text information>, image summary: <neighbor image
            summary> (or, if unavailable: ’No co-commented post information is available.’) Questions: Using the post’s caption and image
            summary provided above, along with any co-commented data, generate a concise yet informative description of the post.
